name: mirror_weld_scope_divergence
description: Which pairs a mirror's weld is allowed to join. CLOSED by task 1220; the declared gap is empty in the vertex AND the face channel and the runner recomputes both live. Base: a quad plus a triangle whose corner (1.0005, 0, 0.0005) sits 7.071e-4 from the quad's corner (1,0,0). Mirrored through x = 0 with weld distance 1e-3, the reference returns 10 vertices, keeping BOTH images (-1,0,0) and (-1.0005,0,0.0005); as measured we returned 9, having welded that pair into one, and the mirrored triangle's ring lost its own corner with them. NOTE, and it corrects the ledger row that prompted this fixture: the pair in question is 7.071e-4 apart, which is INSIDE 1e-3 under a strict AND a non-strict comparison, so this cell does not measure a threshold comparison at all. What it measures is SCOPE -- our weld considered the freshly created images against each other, the reference's does not join two images of two distinct source vertices. The fix states that as its own parameter: `weldCoincidentVertices(..., pairsMustCrossBound: true)` makes a pair eligible only when exactly one of its two indices is a fresh image. That reading of the MECHANISM is still an INFERENCE from this one cell; the frozen numbers are the measurement.
source: Reference side: headless command-port capture of the mirror command with axis x, centre 0, merge on, fixed range, distance 1e-3 (dirty-geometry sweep, task 1123, case mirr_x_neardup). vibe3d side: live drive of this build.

provenance.notes: INSTRUMENT: the reference side is a BEHAVIOURAL CAPTURE driven through the reference editor's own headless command port -- no display, no pointer, no debugger and no static read of its binary; every number in `reference` is a coordinate the reference itself printed after running the operation on the mesh in `input`. The vibe3d side is a LIVE DRIVE of this build over the HTTP test API through the very steps this fixture stores, read back from /api/model. Both engines are given the SAME base mesh (the reference's own dump, injected verbatim) and the selection travels by COORDINATE, so no element index is assumed to mean the same thing on both sides. Nothing here is an inference about the reference's internals; where a MECHANISM is guessed at, the case note says so in that word.

cases.name: two_images_of_a_near_duplicate_pair
cases.note: CLOSED by task 1220. 10 vertices, 13 edges, 4 faces on both sides -- both (-1,0,0) and (-1.0005,0,0.0005) survive, and the mirrored triangle's ring is (-1.0005,0,0.0005)-(-1,0,1)-(-2,0,1) on both. As measured before the fix we returned 9 vertices and 12 edges, (-1.0005,0,0.0005) welded away. The source pair (1,0,0)/(1.0005,0,0.0005), 7.071e-4 apart, survives intact on both sides and always did; only their images ever differed.
